```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelr)
library(lubridate)
```

## Load data

```{r}
trips_per_day <-
    read_tsv("trips_per_day_2015.tsv")

weather <-
    read_csv("weather_2015.csv") %>%
    mutate(ymd = DATE, snow = SNOW, snwd = SNWD, tmin = TMIN*.1, tmax = TMAX*.1, prcp = PRCP, month = mday(ymd), weekend = (wday(ymd, week_start = 7) == 1 | wday(ymd) == 6 | wday(ymd) == 7)) %>%
    select(ymd, tmin, tmax, snow, prcp, snwd, month, weekend)

trips_with_weather <-
    inner_join(trips_per_day, weather, by = "ymd")

load("C:/Users/chana/Documents/coursework/week3/final_model.RData")

rmse(final_model, trips_with_weather)
rsquare(final_model, trips_with_weather)
RMSE <- sqrt(mean((predict(final_model, trips_with_weather) - trips_with_weather$num_trips)^2))
RMSE

ggplot(trips_with_weather, aes(x = num_trips, y = predict(final_model, trips_with_weather))) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_abline(na.rm =TRUE) +
    xlab("Number of Trips (actual value)") +
    ylab("Predicted Number of Trips")
```

## Results

My RMSE in my cross validation was 4608.399, while it was 8578.844 on the 2015 data.
I think that my model could have fit better than it did, but considering the risks of 
overfitting because people's behavior can never be fully predicted, I think this model 
did pretty well, with an rsquared value of 0.6841944.
